subject.title: iOS: keychain save fails on fresh install (cal save failed / disconnected because it could not securely save)

question: After a signed-device reproduction identifies the OSStatus, which Keychain entitlement, accessibility, or item-lifecycle change preserves the intended credential security boundary across fresh installs and upgrades?
rationale: The issue is urgent, but selecting a storage workaround before identifying the native failure could weaken token protection or create an upgrade-only regression.

options.title: Diagnose then repair Keychain
options.body: Capture the signed-device OSStatus and entitlement state, then make the narrow native persistence correction with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Ship an in-app recovery flow
options.body: Add retry and actionable diagnostics without changing storage semantics if the failure proves environmental rather than an application defect.

options.title: Accept weaker fallback storage
options.body: Permit onboarding to continue using non-Keychain storage, intentionally reducing credential protection.

recommendation.title: Diagnose then repair Keychain
recommendation.body: Capture the signed-device OSStatus and entitlement state, then make the narrow native persistence correction with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing signal for the iOS area and are already subscribed to this report.
